nodes.title: Owned software
nodes.description: This profile applies to code and executable behavior that the assessed team builds or maintains. It includes a release whose behavior changes when code behind an existing control is enabled. It does not include a change to the control's value, which is S4, or a change to deployment assembly, which is S3.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor removes controls that do not fit the changed code path and records the reason. For example, a pure formatting change may not need capacity testing, while a payment mutation needs the persistent-state and correctness controls in this profile.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T01, T02, T04, T05, T09: Owned behavior needs focused, integrated, installed-release, capacity, and boundary testing as the path requires. Evidence: Test definitions, results, and release checks.

R01, R04, R05, R08, R09: Code changes need peer review, and structural, policy, or security review when their vector makes it relevant. Evidence: Review records and change proposals.

V01, V02, V08, V16: A releasable build needs traceability, static checks, readiness validation, and verified inputs. Evidence: Build records, analysis output, and readiness gates.

G01, G04: A new executable should receive limited exposure and measured gating when its user impact is material. Evidence: Release plans, cohort records, and gate signals.

D01, D02, D03, D04, D05, D14, D16: User outcomes, release regressions, active checks, diagnostic context, and efficiency need detection. Evidence: Objectives, dashboards, alerts, traces, and cost records.

A01, A04, A05, A07, A08, A09: The service should contain unsafe code behavior through reversal, load protection, and dependency containment where relevant. Evidence: Rollback rules and runtime configuration.

O01, O04, O05, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need a rollback, demand-control, disable, ownership, escalation, and exercised response path. Evidence: Runbooks, ownership records, exercises, and incident records.

H01, H02, H12, H15, H16, H17, H18, H19, H20, H21, H22: Code paths can need artifact control, isolation, safe degradation, correctness semantics, and data protection by design. Evidence: Architecture records, source, policies, and system configuration.

nodes.title: API and business behavior
nodes.description: Request, API, business-rule, or algorithm behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add capacity, request-boundary, persistent-state, security, or correctness controls for the changed behavior.

nodes.title: Business-rule revision
nodes.description: A release changes a calculation, eligibility rule, or other decision visible to users.

nodes.title: API response revision
nodes.description: A release changes the fields, status codes, or ordering returned by an endpoint.

nodes.title: Jobs and workers
nodes.description: Background-job, worker, scheduler, or batch-processing code changes.
nodes.guidance: Add recovery controls when the worker changes persistent state or failover behavior.

nodes.title: Schedule logic revision
nodes.description: A worker release changes when a job runs, how work is selected, or which tasks are skipped.

nodes.title: Batch-processing revision
nodes.description: A release changes batching, checkpointing, or how a partially completed job resumes.

nodes.title: Data and persistence code
nodes.description: Data-access, caching, serialization, or persistent-state handling code changes.
nodes.guidance: Add access and data-protection controls for sensitive or regulated state.

nodes.title: Serialization revision
nodes.description: A release changes the representation of stored or transmitted data.

nodes.title: Cache behavior revision
nodes.description: A release changes cache keys, expiry, invalidation, or the conditions that allow a cached result.

nodes.title: Errors and recovery
nodes.description: Error handling, retry, recovery, or degradation behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add persistent-state recovery controls when the error path can corrupt or lose state.

nodes.title: Retry-policy revision
nodes.description: A release changes retry timing, attempt limits, or which errors are retried.

nodes.title: Fallback-path revision
nodes.description: A release changes which result or service is used when the normal path fails.

nodes.title: Performance and concurrency
nodes.description: Performance, concurrency, queueing, memory, or resource-use behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add correctness controls when overload can repeat, reorder, or race work.

nodes.title: Locking revision
nodes.description: A release changes synchronization, lock ordering, or access to shared state.

nodes.title: Allocation revision
nodes.description: A release changes memory allocation, object lifetime, buffering, or resource retention.

nodes.title: Security and data handling
nodes.description: Authorization, secret handling, sensitive-data handling, or audit behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add request-boundary controls when the changed code receives untrusted requests.

nodes.title: Authorization-check revision
nodes.description: A release changes the code that determines whether a caller can perform an operation.

nodes.title: Sensitive-data handling revision
nodes.description: A release changes how secrets or personal data are logged, stored, transformed, or returned.

nodes.title: Generated behavior and models
nodes.description: Generated code, owned models, rulesets, or other executable behavior owned by the team.
nodes.guidance: Add the controls for the behavior class that generated code or a model changes.

nodes.title: Model release
nodes.description: An owned model version changes the predictions or decisions produced by the system.

nodes.title: Generated-code revision
nodes.description: A generator or its input changes executable code that the team builds and ships.

nodes.title: Consumed software
nodes.description: This profile applies to libraries, frameworks, SDKs, language runtimes, plugins, and transitive packages that execute in the system process. It does not cover a remote service that the system calls, which is S9, or the declaration that assembles an installed image, which is S3.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor classifies a base image or deployment manifest under S3 when its assembled artifact, rather than its in-process library behavior, is the changed support-boundary element.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T02, T03, T04, T06: Consumed code needs integrated, contract, installed-release, and fault-path evidence where its behavior is material. Evidence: Test results, contract suites, and release checks.

R01, R06, R07, R08, R09: Version changes need peer, dependency, compatibility, policy, and security review as their scope requires. Evidence: Dependency-change records and review history.

V01, V02, V12, V13, V14, V15, V16: The build, interfaces, dependency access, credentials, and package integrity need verification. Evidence: Dependency declarations, build records, compatibility checks, and provenance records.

G01, G04, G05: A dependency release should receive limited exposure, measured gates, and ordered rollout when consumers differ. Evidence: Release cohorts and rollout records.

D01, D02, D04, D09, D10, D14, D15: User outcomes, release effects, dependency behavior, diagnosis, and access events need detection. Evidence: Dashboards, alerts, traces, and audit records.

A01, A07, A08, A09, A10: The system should reverse unsafe versions and contain or route around bad dependency behavior where possible. Evidence: Rollback records and runtime resilience configuration.

O01, O08, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need a release rollback, dependency-failover, documented, owned, escalated, and exercised path. Evidence: Runbooks, owner records, and exercise evidence.

H01, H02, H07, H12, H13, H20, H21, H22: Immutable assembly, version declaration, isolation, fallback, access, secret, and data protections can limit harm. Evidence: Artifact policy, architecture records, and access configuration.

nodes.title: Direct packages
nodes.description: A direct library, framework, SDK, or plugin version changes.
nodes.guidance: Add dependency containment when the library calls external services or changes persistent state.

nodes.title: SDK upgrade
nodes.description: A direct SDK version changes the behavior of calls made by the system.

nodes.title: Framework upgrade
nodes.description: A framework upgrade changes routing, lifecycle, defaults, or integration behavior.

nodes.title: Transitive packages and runtimes
nodes.description: A transitive package, runtime, or generated dependency version changes.
nodes.guidance: Add installed-release testing when transitive behavior cannot be isolated in lower-level tests.

nodes.title: Transitive dependency update
nodes.description: A dependency of a direct package changes, possibly without a change to the declared direct version.

nodes.title: Language-runtime upgrade
nodes.description: A language runtime version changes parsing, scheduling, garbage collection, or standard-library behavior.

nodes.title: Compatibility and resource use
nodes.description: A compatibility, behavior, performance, or resource-use change occurs in consumed code.
nodes.guidance: Add failover or recovery controls when behavior changes a serving or state path.

nodes.title: Dependency-default revision
nodes.description: Consumed code changes a default such as a timeout, encoding, or connection setting.

nodes.title: Dependency resource-use revision
nodes.description: Consumed code changes its memory, CPU, thread, or connection requirements.

nodes.title: Provenance, security, and licensing
nodes.description: A consumed package changes its security, provenance, or licensing properties.
nodes.guidance: Add privacy controls when the package can process sensitive data.

nodes.title: Package provenance change
nodes.description: A package changes publisher, build source, signing identity, or delivery channel.

nodes.title: Vulnerable package discovery
nodes.description: New information changes the security status of an already consumed package.

nodes.title: Extensions and agents
nodes.description: A runtime extension, agent, or in-process integration changes its behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add the controls for the interaction or workload behavior that the extension changes.

nodes.title: Instrumentation-agent update
nodes.description: An in-process tracing or metrics agent changes interception, buffering, or runtime overhead.

nodes.title: Plugin update
nodes.description: A loaded plugin changes behavior or its integration with the host process.

nodes.title: Deployment artifacts
nodes.description: This profile applies to declarations and automation that assemble, deploy, start, schedule, or health-check the system without being its application logic. It does not cover effective runtime configuration or data values, which are S4, or underlying platform behavior, which is S5.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor places a managed-platform outage under S5 even when an S3 artifact selected the platform resource that later failed.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T07, T10: A support artifact needs failover evidence when it controls serving paths and dry-run evidence before it changes an environment. Evidence: Exercise records, plans, and dry-run output.

R03, R04, R05, R08: Deployment and infrastructure artifacts need peer, capacity, resilience, and policy review as their scope requires. Evidence: Change reviews and infrastructure proposals.

V06, V07, V08, V16: Declarations, plans, readiness, and input integrity need validation before deployment. Evidence: Validation output, release records, and provenance data.

G03, G04: Infrastructure or topology changes need limited exposure and measured gates when their blast radius is material. Evidence: Cohort records, change windows, and gate signals.

D04, D06, D12, D14: Release effects, platform health, deployment drift, and diagnostic context need observation. Evidence: Deployment-aware dashboards, configuration records, and traces.

A01, A02, A03, A10: The system should reverse unsafe artifacts, restore capacity, or route away from an unsafe path where possible. Evidence: Automation rules and response history.

O01, O06, O07, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need rollback, capacity, quarantine, documented, owned, escalated, and exercised paths. Evidence: Runbooks, records, and exercise evidence.

H01, H04, H05, H15: Immutable artifacts, redundant capacity, fault-domain separation, and bounded deployment scope contain an artifact change. Evidence: Artifact policy, topology records, and deployment configuration.

nodes.title: Build and assembly
nodes.description: Build, package, image, or artifact-assembly definitions change.
nodes.guidance: Add capacity or topology controls when assembly changes resource placement or scale.

nodes.title: Base-image revision
nodes.description: An image definition selects a different operating-system base or installed package set.

nodes.title: Compiler-option revision
nodes.description: A build definition changes optimization, linking, target architecture, or feature flags.

nodes.title: Release and startup
nodes.description: Deployment manifests, release workflows, startup scripts, or initialization automation change.
nodes.guidance: Add failover and degradation controls when startup or release automation controls a serving path.

nodes.title: Release-workflow revision
nodes.description: A deployment workflow changes gates, artifact selection, or the order of rollout steps.

nodes.title: Startup-script revision
nodes.description: Initialization automation changes environment setup, migrations, or readiness behavior.

nodes.title: Scheduling and discovery
nodes.description: Scheduling, scaling, health-check, or service-discovery declarations change.
nodes.guidance: Add workload isolation and overload controls when health or scaling changes shared capacity.

nodes.title: Health-check declaration revision
nodes.description: A deployment artifact changes a readiness or liveness check, threshold, or timing value.

nodes.title: Resource declaration revision
nodes.description: A manifest changes resource requests, limits, replicas, or placement constraints.

nodes.title: Infrastructure declarations
nodes.description: Infrastructure-as-code, topology declarations, or bootstrap automation change.
nodes.guidance: Add durable-state controls when the declaration changes storage or replication.

nodes.title: Topology-template revision
nodes.description: Infrastructure-as-code changes the declared network, storage, or serving topology.

nodes.title: Bootstrap declaration revision
nodes.description: Provisioning automation changes how a host or resource is initialized.

nodes.title: Deployment identity and provenance
nodes.description: Build or deployment identity, permission, or artifact-provenance configuration changes.
nodes.guidance: Add credential rotation controls when deployment identity changes.

nodes.title: Pipeline-permission revision
nodes.description: Deployment configuration changes what the build or release identity can access.

nodes.title: Artifact-verification revision
nodes.description: A release definition changes signature checks, provenance checks, or trusted artifact sources.

nodes.title: Controlled runtime state
nodes.description: This profile applies to state that changes the behavior or protection of the support boundary without changing its executable code. It includes configuration, flags, data, schemas, access policy, partition maps, and credential configuration. It does not include a code change that reads that state, which is S1.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor may split one source S4 row into separate rows for flags, data, access policy, and credentials when those classes have different owners or change paths.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T02, T04, T08, T11: Controlled state needs integrated, installed-release, restore, and migration evidence as its vector requires. Evidence: Test results, exercises, and migration records.

R02, R07, R08, R09: State changes need peer, compatibility, policy, and security review when they affect users or protection. Evidence: Change records and review history.

V03, V04, V05, V15: Configuration syntax, configuration semantics, state compatibility, and credential readiness need validation. Evidence: Validators, migration checks, and credential records.

G02, G04, G06, G07: State should move through limited activation, gates, staged rotation, and reversible migration increments. Evidence: Flag history, cohort records, and migration plans.

D01, D02, D05, D11, D12, D13, D14, D15: User outcomes, active checks, effective state, drift, integrity, diagnosis, and security actions need observation. Evidence: Dashboards, audit records, reconciliation, and traces.

A01, A11: The system should reverse an unsafe state change or renew credentials before it causes service loss where possible. Evidence: Revert automation and credential rotation records.

O02, O05, O09, O10, O11, O12, O13: Operators need a state-revert, disable, owned, escalated, exercised, and data-repair path. Evidence: Runbooks, owners, incident records, and exercises.

H03, H06, H14, H16, H17, H18, H19, H20, H21, H22, H23: State needs safe stale behavior, durable recovery, correctness semantics, and protection controls by design. Evidence: Architecture, storage configuration, access policy, and retention records.

nodes.title: Flags, limits, and routing
nodes.description: Feature flags, dynamic configuration, limits, quotas, or routing rules change.
nodes.guidance: Add demand, tenant-isolation, or access controls when the state changes them.

nodes.title: Feature-flag toggle
nodes.description: A live flag value enables, disables, or changes exposure to code that is already deployed.

nodes.title: Runtime-limit revision
nodes.description: An operator changes a live timeout, quota, concurrency limit, or routing weight.

nodes.title: Schemas and records
nodes.description: Schemas, indexes, records, migrations, backfills, or data repairs change.
nodes.guidance: Add data-protection and retention controls for sensitive or regulated records.

nodes.title: Schema migration
nodes.description: An operation changes the structure, constraints, or indexes of persisted data.

nodes.title: Data backfill
nodes.description: An operation creates or revises existing records outside the normal request path.

nodes.title: Partitioning and retention
nodes.description: Partition maps, shard assignments, replication settings, or retention rules change.
nodes.guidance: Add compatibility controls when clients observe the partitioning change.

nodes.title: Shard reassignment
nodes.description: A runtime map changes which partition or replica owns a set of records.

nodes.title: Retention-policy revision
nodes.description: A runtime policy changes when data expires, is archived, or is deleted.

nodes.title: Access policy and secrets
nodes.description: Access policy, authorization mappings, secret references, or credential configuration changes.
nodes.guidance: Add staged rotation controls when an identity or credential changes.

nodes.title: Permission-policy revision
nodes.description: An operator changes authorization mappings or permissions in the control plane.

nodes.title: Secret-reference revision
nodes.description: A configuration value points running software at a different secret or credential version.

nodes.title: Keys and certificates
nodes.description: Certificates, keys, or identity-configuration state changes.
nodes.guidance: Add provider dependency controls when a certificate or identity authority is external.

nodes.title: Certificate rotation
nodes.description: An operation changes the certificate, issuer, or trust configuration used by the system.

nodes.title: Encryption-key rotation
nodes.description: An operation changes the key used to encrypt, decrypt, or sign data.

nodes.title: Infrastructure and platform
nodes.description: This profile applies to the hosts, containers, storage, networks, name resolution, capacity, regions, zones, routing topology, operating systems, and managed-platform behavior that support the system. It covers a consumed resource that changes or fails without being called as an application dependency. A remote service called by the system is S9.
nodes.guidance:
The profile does not require multi-region or multi-zone deployment for every service. The assessor records the required availability, data durability, and fault-domain coverage before it judges these controls.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T05, T06, T07, T10: Capacity, fault, failover, and declaration paths need exercised evidence. Evidence: Test results, game-day records, and dry-run output.

R03, R04, R05, R08: Support artifacts and structural changes need peer, capacity, resilience, and policy review. Evidence: Change proposals and review records.

V06, V07, V08: Infrastructure declarations, plans, and readiness need validation. Evidence: Plan output, readiness checks, and release records.

G03, G04: A topology or platform change needs limited exposure and measured gates when possible. Evidence: Change plans, cohorts, and gate signals.

D01, D02, D06, D07, D12, D16: User outcomes, platform health, capacity, drift, and efficiency need observation. Evidence: Objectives, dashboards, declarations, and cost records.

A02, A03, A04, A05, A08, A09, A10: The system should replace, scale, protect, contain, or route around unhealthy capacity without waiting for an operator. Evidence: Automation rules and response records.

O03, O04, O06, O07, O08, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need failover, demand, capacity, quarantine, degradation, and exercised response paths. Evidence: Runbooks, owner records, and exercises.

H04, H05, H06, H07, H08, H09, H10, H11, H12, H13, H15: Redundancy, fault isolation, durable state, bounded work, fairness, fallback, and cells contain infrastructure change. Evidence: Architecture, topology, resource policy, and storage records.

nodes.title: Compute and hosts
nodes.description: Compute capacity, placement, container runtime, or host behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add state and recovery controls when compute loss can lose persistent work.

nodes.title: Host loss
nodes.description: A compute host stops executing the software because of failure, eviction, or maintenance.

nodes.title: Compute-shape change
nodes.description: The platform changes available CPU, memory, architecture, or execution limits.

nodes.title: Storage behavior
nodes.description: Storage availability, performance, replication, or durability behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add migration controls when the storage format or schema changes.

nodes.title: Storage-latency shift
nodes.description: A storage resource has a change in latency or throughput without an application release.

nodes.title: Storage availability loss
nodes.description: A disk, volume, or managed storage path becomes unavailable to the running system.

nodes.title: Network and name resolution
nodes.description: Network connectivity, routing, name resolution, or certificate-transport behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add certificate and identity controls when the transport trust path changes.

nodes.title: Network partition
nodes.description: Connectivity changes so that some peers are reachable while others are isolated.

nodes.title: DNS resolution change
nodes.description: Name resolution returns different addresses, fails, or has a change in caching behavior.

nodes.title: Regions and fault domains
nodes.description: Region, zone, fault-domain, or topology availability changes.
nodes.guidance: Add workload-containment controls when the fault-domain event can overload survivors.

nodes.title: Zone outage
nodes.description: A fault-domain event removes compute, network, or storage availability in one zone.

nodes.title: Regional impairment
nodes.description: A regional event changes the availability or capacity of serving and recovery resources.

nodes.title: Managed-platform behavior
nodes.description: Managed-platform release, quota, scaling, or control-plane behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add dependency controls when the platform is outside the support boundary.

nodes.title: Platform rollout
nodes.description: A provider release changes orchestration, admission, or the behavior of a managed platform.

nodes.title: Platform quota change
nodes.description: A platform quota changes the amount or rate of resource allocation available to the system.

nodes.title: Demand and transport
nodes.description: This profile applies when demand changes independently of what requests mean. It includes benign and malicious traffic. It does not cover a payload, operation, or parameter combination that makes one request expensive or unsafe, which is S7.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor records the workload class and the expected demand bound before judging a rate, capacity, or fairness control as absent or partial.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T05, T06: Demand protection needs capacity and overload-fault evidence. Evidence: Load-test results and overload exercises.

D01, D02, D03, D05, D07, D14, D16: Objectives, user outcomes, alerts, probes, demand, diagnosis, and efficiency need observation. Evidence: Objectives, dashboards, alerts, traces, and cost records.

A03, A04, A05: The system should scale, limit admission, or shed load when demand exceeds safe bounds. Evidence: Autoscaling and overload-control configuration.

O03, O04, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need traffic, demand, documented, owned, escalated, and exercised response paths. Evidence: Runbooks, owner records, and exercises.

H04, H07, H08, H09, H10, H11, H12, H16, H17, H18, H19: Redundancy, workload isolation, bounded work, fairness, degradation, and correctness semantics contain overload. Evidence: Architecture, resource policy, queues, and request-handling code.

nodes.title: Sustained growth
nodes.description: Sustained request-rate, concurrency, or connection-count growth occurs.
nodes.guidance: Add cost monitoring and manual traffic shifting for sustained growth that can exceed planned capacity.

nodes.title: Request-rate growth
nodes.description: The arrival rate remains above its former baseline long enough to require a capacity response.

nodes.title: Concurrent-connection growth
nodes.description: The number of simultaneous connections or in-flight requests increases over time.

nodes.title: Bursts and storms
nodes.description: A burst, retry storm, recovery surge, or thundering herd occurs.
nodes.guidance: Add retry and idempotency controls when the surge can repeat work.

nodes.title: Retry storm
nodes.description: Clients repeat failed requests together, increasing demand while the system is already impaired.

nodes.title: Recovery surge
nodes.description: Queued or deferred clients return together after an outage or service restoration.

nodes.title: Traffic distribution
nodes.description: Traffic distribution becomes skewed across tenants, keys, regions, or serving paths.
nodes.guidance: Add cells or partitions when skew can produce a broad blast radius.

nodes.title: Tenant traffic skew
nodes.description: One tenant accounts for a growing share of request volume, independent of request meaning.

nodes.title: Regional traffic shift
nodes.description: Traffic moves between regions or serving paths and changes their relative load.

nodes.title: Connection behavior
nodes.description: Connection lifetime, protocol behavior, retransmission, or transport churn changes.
nodes.guidance: Add deadline and connection-containment controls when transport waits on downstream work.

nodes.title: Connection churn
nodes.description: Clients create and discard connections at a rate that changes transport overhead.

nodes.title: Long-lived connection growth
nodes.description: Connections stay open longer and occupy sockets, memory, or other transport resources.

nodes.title: Client transport policy
nodes.description: A client population changes retry, timeout, caching, or reconnect behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add client-specific compatibility controls when retry behavior is an interface contract.

nodes.title: Client retry-policy change
nodes.description: A client population changes retry timing or attempts without a server release.

nodes.title: Cache-bypass behavior
nodes.description: Clients stop using local or intermediary caches and send more requests to the origin.

nodes.title: Abuse and denial of service
nodes.description: Abusive or denial-of-service demand changes the load on the service.
nodes.guidance: Add security review and audit controls when abusive traffic has a security dimension.

nodes.title: Request flood
nodes.description: An actor sends enough requests to change the service demand or available capacity.

nodes.title: Connection-exhaustion attempt
nodes.description: An actor holds or creates connections to consume transport resources.

nodes.title: Request meaning
nodes.description: This profile applies when a request's content, operation, or semantic combination changes the work that the system performs. It differs from S6, which concerns rate and transport behavior without regard to request meaning.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor treats a request as both S6 and S7 when its arrival rate and its meaning each need different controls.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T02, T09: Request behavior needs integrated and negative-path evidence where it can reach state or dependencies. Evidence: Integration suites, boundary tests, and results.

R07, R09: Interface and protection changes need compatibility and security or privacy review. Evidence: Interface proposals and review records.

V09, V10, V11: The boundary needs structural, authorization, and semantic validation. Evidence: Boundary code, schemas, policies, and test results.

D01, D02, D03, D08, D14, D15, D16: User outcomes, alerts, abusive patterns, diagnosis, audit activity, and efficiency need observation. Evidence: Dashboards, traces, audit records, and cost signals.

A04, A05, A06: The system should limit admission, shed unsafe work, or reject dangerous requests. Evidence: Admission policy and request-handling configuration.

O04, O05, O09, O10, O11, O12: Operators need demand, disable, documented, owned, escalated, and exercised response paths. Evidence: Runbooks, ownership records, and exercises.

H07, H08, H09, H10, H11, H12, H16, H17, H18, H19, H20, H21, H22, H23: Isolation, bounded work, safe behavior, correctness semantics, access, data, and retention controls limit request harm. Evidence: Architecture, source, policies, and data-handling records.

nodes.title: Structure and size
nodes.description: A request has an invalid, malformed, oversized, deeply nested, or unsupported structure.
nodes.guidance: Add authorization and audit controls when malformed requests can cross a protection boundary.

nodes.title: Payload-size increase
nodes.description: An individual request carries a larger body or collection than the system normally processes.

nodes.title: Malformed or nested payload
nodes.description: A request has invalid syntax, unsupported structure, or nesting that changes parsing work.

nodes.title: Operation cost
nodes.description: A parameter, query shape, filter, aggregation, or operation has an unsafe cost.
nodes.guidance: Add tenant isolation when a costly operation can consume shared capacity.

nodes.title: Unbounded query
nodes.description: A request omits limits or selects a query plan that has work beyond the expected bound.

nodes.title: Expensive aggregation
nodes.description: A request asks for a combination of filters or aggregations that increases computation per call.

nodes.title: Target skew
nodes.description: A request targets a hot key, tenant, partition, or other skewed resource.
nodes.guidance: Add partition and cell controls when a hot target has a broad blast radius.

nodes.title: Hot-key request
nodes.description: A request targets a key that has contention or work concentrated on one resource.

nodes.title: Tenant-wide operation
nodes.description: One request spans a tenant or partition and concentrates work despite a normal request rate.

nodes.title: Versions and combinations
nodes.description: A request presents an unsupported version, combination of fields, or compatibility state.
nodes.guidance: Add ordered rollout controls when versions must coexist.

nodes.title: Unsupported API version
nodes.description: A request names an interface version that the receiving system does not support.

nodes.title: Unexpected field combination
nodes.description: Individually valid fields appear together in a combination the system does not handle.

nodes.title: Repetition and ordering
nodes.description: A request repeats, reorders, races, or replays an operation with persistent effects.
nodes.guidance: Add persistent-state recovery controls when repeated work can cause data loss or corruption.

nodes.title: Duplicate state-changing request
nodes.description: A client repeats an operation that has persistent effects, with or without an idempotency key.

nodes.title: Concurrent conflicting requests
nodes.description: Requests race or arrive out of order while changing the same state.

nodes.title: Protection boundaries
nodes.description: A request crosses an authorization, privacy, retention, or policy boundary.
nodes.guidance: Add compatibility controls when protection policy changes affect existing clients.

nodes.title: Cross-tenant access attempt
nodes.description: A request attempts to access or change a resource owned by another tenant.

nodes.title: Restricted-data request
nodes.description: A request asks for data or an operation outside the caller’s privacy or retention boundary.

nodes.title: Usage assumptions
nodes.description: A new client usage pattern changes semantic assumptions without changing aggregate demand.
nodes.guidance: Add the controls for each concrete request behavior the new usage exposes.

nodes.title: New operation sequence
nodes.description: Clients use valid operations in an order that exposes an assumption in the service.

nodes.title: New locale or time pattern
nodes.description: Client inputs introduce locale, calendar, or time-zone cases that change request interpretation.

nodes.title: Internal interactions
nodes.description: This profile applies to calls, messages, replication, coordination, control-plane commands, and health checks among components inside the unit of supportability. It does not cover a call to a service outside that boundary, which is S9.
nodes.guidance:
The assessor separates caller and callee rows when they have different owners, evidence, or control paths, even when they participate in the same interaction.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T02, T03, T05, T06, T07, T08: Internal paths need integration, contract, load, fault, failover, and recovery evidence as their vector requires. Evidence: Test results and exercise records.

R04, R05, R07, R08: Capacity, resilience, compatibility, and high-impact change review apply to material interaction paths. Evidence: Architecture proposals and review records.

V08, V12: Serving readiness and interface compatibility need validation before normal traffic. Evidence: Readiness gates and compatibility checks.

G04, G05: Measured gates and ordered producer-consumer rollout contain compatibility changes. Evidence: Rollout plans and gate records.

D01, D02, D03, D05, D09, D10, D13, D14: Outcomes, alerts, probes, dependency behavior, integrity, and request diagnosis need observation. Evidence: Objectives, dashboards, traces, and reconciliation records.

A07, A08, A09, A10: Retries, deadlines, circuit containment, and traffic shifts protect interaction paths. Evidence: Client configuration and automation records.

O03, O08, O09, O10, O11, O12, O13: Operators need failover, degraded operation, documentation, ownership, escalation, exercises, and data repair. Evidence: Runbooks, owners, and exercise records.

H06, H07, H08, H09, H10, H11, H12, H13, H16, H17, H18, H19: Durable state, isolation, bounded work, fallback, and correctness semantics contain internal propagation. Evidence: Architecture records, queues, and state-handling code.

nodes.title: Calls and fanout
nodes.description: A synchronous call, fanout, or service-to-service request path changes behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add recovery and durable-state controls when the call performs a state mutation.

nodes.title: Fanout expansion
nodes.description: An internal request contacts more components or performs more downstream calls than before.

nodes.title: Internal deadline mismatch
nodes.description: The caller and callee have deadline behavior that changes cancellation or completion semantics.

nodes.title: Queues and streams
nodes.description: A queue, stream, event, or scheduled asynchronous path changes timing or delivery behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add a replay and data-repair path when messages have persistent effects.

nodes.title: Message-delivery delay
nodes.description: An internal queue or stream delivers work later and changes processing order or backlog.

nodes.title: Redelivery behavior change
nodes.description: An internal message path changes acknowledgement or delivery behavior and repeats work.

nodes.title: Consistency and replay
nodes.description: Replication, caching, consistency, ordering, duplication, or replay behavior changes.
nodes.guidance: Add data-protection controls when replication or caching handles sensitive data.

nodes.title: Replication lag
nodes.description: Internal replicas fall further behind and change the freshness of served data.

nodes.title: Event replay
nodes.description: An internal replay repeats historical operations or messages against current state.

nodes.title: Version compatibility
nodes.description: Producer and consumer versions become incompatible or roll out in a different order.
nodes.guidance: Add a compatibility test across every producer and consumer version in scope.

nodes.title: Producer-first rollout
nodes.description: A producer emits a new format before all consumers can accept it.

nodes.title: Consumer contract divergence
nodes.description: An internal consumer changes its assumptions while an older producer continues to run.

nodes.title: Coordination and health
nodes.description: Health checks, leader election, coordination, or control-plane commands behave differently.
nodes.guidance: Add durable-state recovery when the coordination path protects persistent assignments or state.

nodes.title: Leader-election churn
nodes.description: Internal coordination changes leaders often enough to affect serving or state ownership.

nodes.title: Health-check disagreement
nodes.description: Components have different views of readiness and route work to an unsuitable peer.

nodes.title: Failure propagation
nodes.description: An internal workload becomes saturated and propagates delay or failure to another component.
nodes.guidance: Add traffic shifting when the saturated path has independent serving alternatives.

nodes.title: Queue saturation
nodes.description: An internal workload fills a queue or work pool and delays other components.

nodes.title: Shared-pool exhaustion
nodes.description: One component consumes a connection, thread, or memory pool used by other paths.

nodes.title: External dependencies
nodes.description: This profile applies to remote services, data stores, identity providers, certificate authorities, and other resources outside the unit of supportability. It covers availability, latency, contract, credential, data, and semantic changes in those dependencies. It does not cover an in-process library, which is S2.
nodes.guidance:
The agent assesses client-owned controls, such as deadlines, retries, circuit containment, fallback, interface validation, dependency monitoring, and an operator response path, directly. It treats a provider's durability, backup, repair, retention, or regional-recovery capability as a guarantee that needs supplied contract, architecture, or exercise evidence. The agent records such a guarantee as unknown when that evidence is unavailable; it does not claim that the client implements the provider's control.

The agent excludes a provider control only when the support-boundary statement says that the service does not rely on the capability for an in-scope user outcome. A dependency responsibility record names the provider, client, needed guarantee, evidence source, owner, and escalation path.

The assessor creates separate rows for each caller when the same dependency has different timeouts, fallbacks, credentials, data semantics, or user outcomes for different callers.

The source coverage guidance applies when the change vector is unknown.

T02, T03, T06, T07, T08: Dependencies need integration, contract, fault, failover, and recovery evidence as their paths require. Evidence: Test results, contract suites, and exercise records.

R05, R06, R07, R08, R09: Dependency, version, compatibility, policy, and security review apply to material external paths. Evidence: Dependency records and review history.

V12, V13, V14, V15, V16: Interfaces, reachability, permission, credentials, and integration integrity need validation. Evidence: Compatibility checks, connection checks, and provenance records.

G01, G04, G05, G06, G07: Releases, compatibility shifts, credential rotation, and state migration need limited exposure and safe progression. Evidence: Rollout, rotation, and migration records.

D01, D02, D03, D05, D09, D10, D13, D14, D15: Outcomes, alerts, active probes, dependency behavior, integrity, diagnosis, and audit events need observation. Evidence: Objectives, dashboards, probes, traces, and audit records.

A07, A08, A09, A10, A11: Retries, deadlines, circuit containment, traffic shifts, and credential renewal limit dependency harm. Evidence: Client configuration and automation records.

O03, O08, O09, O10, O11, O12, O13: Operators need failover, degraded operation, documentation, ownership, escalation, exercises, and data repair. Evidence: Runbooks, owners, and incident records.

H06, H07, H12, H13, H14, H16, H17, H18, H19, H20, H21, H22, H23: Durable state, isolation, fallback, recovery, correctness, and protection controls limit external dependency impact. Evidence: Architecture, storage, policy, and response records.

nodes.title: Availability and latency
nodes.description: A dependency becomes unavailable, slow, overloaded, or intermittently reachable.
nodes.guidance: Add data repair and recovery evidence when the dependency owns state that the system must recover.

nodes.title: Provider outage
nodes.description: A service outside the support boundary stops completing operations.

nodes.title: Provider latency shift
nodes.description: A dependency response time increases or becomes intermittent without a client release.

nodes.title: Interface contracts
nodes.description: A dependency changes an API, protocol, schema, version, response, or error contract.
nodes.guidance: Add data-protection or state-migration controls when the contract carries persistent or sensitive data.

nodes.title: Provider schema revision
nodes.description: A provider changes a response schema, field representation, or protocol contract.

nodes.title: Provider error-contract revision
nodes.description: A provider changes status codes, error bodies, or which conditions are retryable.

nodes.title: Quotas, cost, and policy
nodes.description: A dependency changes rate limits, quotas, pricing, capacity, or traffic policy.
nodes.guidance: Add traffic shifting when an alternate dependency or serving path exists.

nodes.title: Provider rate-limit revision
nodes.description: A provider changes a rate limit, quota window, or admission policy.

nodes.title: Provider pricing revision
nodes.description: A provider changes the cost of operations, storage, or transferred data.

nodes.title: Identity and trust
nodes.description: A dependency changes credentials, permissions, certificates, identity, or trust behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add fallback or escalation controls when the dependency cannot rotate without a client change.

nodes.title: Provider credential revocation
nodes.description: A provider revokes a credential or changes the permissions attached to it.

nodes.title: Provider trust-chain change
nodes.description: A provider changes certificates, issuers, or identity behavior used by clients.

nodes.title: Returned data
nodes.description: A dependency returns stale, incomplete, inconsistent, or semantically changed data.
nodes.guidance: Add retention and protection controls when returned data is sensitive or regulated.

nodes.title: Stale provider response
nodes.description: A dependency returns data that is older than the client’s required freshness bound.

nodes.title: Provider semantic revision
nodes.description: A provider returns structurally valid data with a changed meaning, completeness, or consistency.

nodes.title: Migration and recovery
nodes.description: A dependency migration, regional event, or recovery event changes its serving behavior.
nodes.guidance: Add provider-guarantee evidence when the event can affect durable data or regional recovery.

nodes.title: Provider regional failover
nodes.description: A provider moves serving to another region and changes latency, consistency, or availability.

nodes.title: Provider restore event
nodes.description: A dependency recovery changes data state or which operations have taken effect.

description:
The catalog defines sources of software change for a unit of supportability: the interface a customer uses or the release a customer installs, together with its components, deployment and control planes, infrastructure, and manual operating procedures. The boundary includes owners and exclusions. Its outcomes can include correctness and data integrity, availability and durability, latency and capacity, security and privacy, compatibility, and resource efficiency.

A change can belong to more than one source when it changes more than one part of that boundary. Classification depends on the element that changes, queue and platform ownership, and the client or provider role. A missing boundary fact is an open classification question.

The categories and subcategories define the scope of the catalog. The kinds of change are proposed examples within that scope; they are not an exhaustive list. A new kind or subcategory is appropriate when a change has a distinct control path. Its description should state that difference. These definitions are editable here and govern subsequent mitigation links and assessments.

mitigations.title: Detection

mitigations.title: Automatic mitigation
mitigations.description: Automatic protections reduce harm without waiting for an operator.

mitigations.title: Operational control
mitigations.description: Operators have response paths and the means to use them.

mitigations.title: Architecture
mitigations.description: Architecture contains failures through system structure.
